summary: Environment A direct binary verification for the Phase 6.3 Windows rebuild (Operator Ergonomics: feed search). Frontend-only change - this file documents what direct binary inspection could and could not confirm, honestly, following the discipline established in Phase 6.1/6.2's own evidence files.

installer.note: The SHA-256 and file size both changed from the Phase 6.2 baseline, confirming a genuinely new artifact was packaged - not a stale/copied installer.

dllPresenceCheck.method: Extracted the installer with 7z and confirmed all three bundled runtime DLLs are present at the installer root.

rustSymbolRegressionCheck.method: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings/nm against the extracted cip-desktop.exe, re-checking every prior-phase Rust-side symbol/string this project's manifest already tracks, to confirm zero Rust regression (this phase touched zero Rust files - confirmed via git status/diff before the rebuild).

result.whisper_full_with_state: 93 occurrences via nm - identical to the Phase 6.2 baseline, including the same breakdown by symbol type (1 global 'T' exported function, 42 't', 31 'r'/.xdata, 19 'p' compiler-generated auxiliary symbols). Unlike the Phase 6.1->6.2 rebuild, this count did not drift at all this time, consistent with Phase 6.2's own explanation that the auxiliary-symbol count is a known, small, build-to-build C++ codegen non-determinism rather than something tied to any particular phase's changes.

rustSymbolRegressionCheck.conclusion: Every previously-tracked Rust-side symbol/string count is unchanged from the Phase 6.2 baseline - confirms zero Rust-side regression, consistent with this phase changing only TypeScript/TSX files.

frontendTextSearchLimitation.attempted: Searched the extracted cip-desktop.exe for this phase's new frontend text: 'Search the feed' (the new search input's placeholder).
frontendTextSearchLimitation.controlExperiment: Also searched for two frontend-only strings known to be present in the source and UNCHANGED by this phase: 'Needs Attention' and 'Intelligence Feed' (the panel's own heading). Both ALSO returned 0 matches, exactly reproducing the Phase 6.1 and 6.2 findings.
frontendTextSearchLimitation.conclusion: Confirms, again, that Tauri's compressed embedded frontend bundle is opaque to plain strings(1)/nm(1) scanning - the same real, already-documented tooling limitation, not a build defect specific to this phase.
correctnessEvidenceUsedInstead: Fresh Vite build produced a new asset bundle hash for this rebuild (dist/assets/index-*.js), distinct from the Phase 6.2 build's bundle - proving a genuinely new frontend bundle was embedded.

Full frontend test suite: 242/242 passing (236 pre-existing + 6 new, covering searchIntelligenceFeed's substring matching, null-safety, whitespace trimming, and empty-query/no-match edge cases) - see pilot-evidence/6.3/build/feed-search-evidence.json.
Installer SHA-256 and file size both changed from the Phase 6.2 baseline (see installer block above), confirming the newly-built bundle was genuinely packaged into this installer.
npm run build (tsc -b && vite build) completed with zero errors as part of the same build pipeline that produced this exact installer.

architectureVerification.outerInstallerStub: PE32 executable (GUI) Intel 80386, Nullsoft Installer self-extracting archive - standard NSIS bootstrapper, unchanged from every prior phase.
architectureVerification.installedApplicationBinary: cip-desktop.exe: PE32+ executable (GUI) x86-64, confirmed genuinely x64.

conclusion: This phase's Rust-side surface is unchanged (confirmed via unchanged symbol/string counts, including whisper_full_with_state's auxiliary-symbol count now matching the Phase 6.2 baseline exactly - the drift seen in the Phase 6.1->6.2 rebuild was not repeated here, further supporting that it was toolchain non-determinism rather than anything phase-specific) and this phase's frontend-side surface is a genuinely new, fully-tested bundle (confirmed via a fresh build hash, a changed installer SHA-256, and a full 242/242 test pass) - but direct strings-based verification of the new frontend text itself is not possible against Tauri's compressed embedded bundle, the same real tooling limitation documented in Phase 6.1/6.2, reproduced here rather than worked around with a fabricated match.
